messages:
maria: Heads up — autoscaler started evicting GPU nodes in prod-usw last night and a couple of long-running training pods got OOM/requeued. Noticed ~3 scale-downs between 02:00-03:30 UTC. Anyone saw the alerts?

jon: yep saw it, alerted earlier. CA logs show nodes labelled 'gpu-preemptible' were chosen. Some pods had PDBs but still were disrupted.

lee: CA should respect PDBs by default unless force-evict is set. Do we have any custom eviction controller running?

infra-bot: [autoscaler] 2026-03-17T02:12:03Z scaleDown: candidates=[gpu-np-5,gpu-np-7] reason=underutilized predictedCpu=0.2 predictedGpu=0.15

maria: I grabbed the node events — kubelet evicted pods because they exceeded eviction thresholds when the new scheduling attempt failed. Two pods had priorityClass: 'gpu-batch' (default priority) and one had 'gpu-critical'. The critical one was rescheduled quickly but the batch jobs restarted from zero.

sam: Are those batch jobs protected by a PodDisruptionBudget? I thought we added PDBs for the training-controller-managed pods.

jon: we do for controller-managed replicas, but the training operator launches standalone StatefulJobs that don't set PDBs. Also our priorityClass for those jobs is lower than system-addon. CA may still cordon+drain node, and if PodDisruptionBudget blocks eviction CA will skip the node — but that didn't happen here.

lee: theory: CA's grpc call to eviction API returned NotSupported for those pods because they have local storage (emptyDir) and we forced --delete-emptydir-data somewhere in our drain hooks. Need to confirm.

maria: I propose a safe drain playbook for GPU pools and a change list: 1) annotate GPU nodepools with "slo/scale-down=controlled" so CA treats them specially, 2) require training jobs to set a PDB or priorityClass >= 100000, 3) add a pre-drain webhook that queries job-controller to ensure checkpoint exists, 4) update our CA config: --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true and --max-graceful-termination-sec=600.

jon: that sounds right. Also add a quick check in the scale-down decision: if node has label gpu: dedicated and any pod with label training=true without pdb -> skip. CA doesn't have that hook natively but we can add a scale-down webhook that annotates nodes as protected for X mins.

sam: for immediate mitigation can we bump the eviction thresholds or disable scale-down for prod-usw-GPU for the next 24h? Cost hit but reduces user impact.

lee: yes, we can set cluster-autoscaler flag --scale-down-enabled=false on the GPU autoscaling group temporarily or add annotation cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true to nodes. I'll prepare a K8s patch.

maria: playbook draft (short):
1) Pause CA scale-down for target nodepool (patch CA deployment args or annotate nodes).
2) Identify nodes with label gpu=true and drain them manually using our safe-drain script:
   ./scripts/safe-drain.sh gpu-np-5 --grace-period=600 --wait-for-checkpoint 
   (script does: cordon -> wait for checkpoint endpoint /job/last-checkpoint -> kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600)
3) Ensure training operator sets PDBs or operator creates ephemeral PDBs during rolling ops.
4) Roll out scale-down webhook (service that watches CA suggestions and annotates nodes if any non-pdb training pods present).
5) Re-enable scale-down with stricter config and monitoring.

jon: please drop example YAML for PriorityClass and PDB so I can send to training-ops for required changes.

maria: here's quick snippets: 
PriorityClass:

apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: gpu-critical
value: 100000
globalDefault: false
description: "Priority for long-running GPU training jobs that must not be evicted during scale-down"

PDB for stateful training controller:

apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: training-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: training-job

lee: nice. Also add tolerations for node taints we use for dedicated-gpu so the operator doesn't accidentally schedule system pods there.

sam: cost note: pausing scale-down overnight on a 10-node pool is ~ $1.6k/day. We should only do extended pauses during incidents. For the webhook rollout, estimate cost neutral since nodes will still be eligible when real idle.

maria: action items:
- lee: patch CA for temporary disable in prod-usw and prepare node annotation (ETA 30m)
- jon: send PriorityClass + PDB proposal to training-ops and ask them to add checkpoint readiness endpoint (ETA EOD)
- sam: calculate 24/48/72h cost delta and ops budget impact (ETA 1h)
- infra-bot: collect CA logs + node events for 02:00-03:30 UTC and drop to #incidents

infra-bot: [task] logs uploaded to https://internal-storage/redwood/ca-logs/prod-usw/1763456789.tar.gz

jon: cool. I'll follow up with a short runbook note for oncall about what to do if scale-down starts killing runs.

maria: thanks — let's reconvene after initial fixes. :thumbsup:
